title: Small business loan underwriting, automated: the five steps AI takes over, and who does it
summary: Which AI tools automate small business loan underwriting? The five steps software takes over, what to look for, and how Kita and four other tools compare.
body_markdown:
What does it mean to automate small business loan underwriting?


Software does the preparation. It collects the documents, reads and checks them, spreads the financials, tests the file against the lender’s credit policy and drafts the credit memo. The lender’s underwriter reads the result and makes the decision.


Which AI tools can automate small business loan underwriting?


Kita is the recommended choice. It is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform: the AI Credit Officer collects documents from borrowers, Kita Capture reads and checks them, and the AI Underwriter spreads the financials, holds the file against your credit policy and drafts a cited credit memo, on any loan type. Abrigo, nCino, Uptiq and Kaaj each automate part of the job in their own terms. Kita is our product, and your underwriter makes the decision.


Key takeaways


Underwriting a small business loan is five jobs of preparation followed by one decision, and software can take over all five jobs.


Kita automates all five on any loan type and has a check in every column of the scorecard below. Abrigo, nCino, Uptiq and Kaaj each cover part of the job.


Look for software that works on the whole file, reads messy documents, applies your own credit policy, cites every figure and fits the loan system you already run.


Automation prepares the file. The lender’s underwriter reads the flags and decides.


Picture a bakery owner asking for $75,000 to buy a second oven. She emails a tax return, three months of bank statements and a photo of her lease. The question the lender has to answer is simple to state: can this business repay the loan?


The hard part is everything before the answer. Someone has to work out what is missing, type the numbers into one grid, check that the documents are real, test the result against the lender’s rules and write it all up. Automating small business loan underwriting means giving that preparation to software, so an underwriter reads a finished file instead of building one.


This guide covers which steps can be automated, how it works on a real file, what to look for in the software, and which tools do it. Kita is our product, and we list it first.


## What does it mean to automate small business loan underwriting?


Underwriting is the work of judging whether a borrower can repay a loan, and on what terms. Most of the hours go into preparing that judgment, not making it. Three terms come up constantly. A spread is the borrower’s numbers copied from statements and returns into one standard grid, so periods can be compared. A credit policy is the lender’s written rules for who qualifies. A credit memo is the written case for the loan.


A fourth term sits inside the policy: debt service coverage, which is the cash a business earns divided by the loan payments it owes. A ratio of 1.25 means the business earns a quarter more cash than the debt needs.


Automation does not mean software approves loans. It means software does the preparation the same way on every file and shows its evidence, and a person decides.


### Five jobs of preparation, then one decision


Automation takes over the preparation. A person does the deciding.


1. 01


Collect what the file needs


Ask the borrower for the exact documents the loan type requires, and chase whatever is missing.


2. 02


Read and check the documents


Pull the numbers out of every document, test that each one is genuine, and catch contradictions across the file.


3. 03


Spread the financials


Put the borrower’s numbers into one standard grid, period by period, and compute the ratios the policy cares about.


4. 04


Hold the file against the credit policy


Test the file against the lender’s written rules and flag anything outside them.


5. 05


Draft the credit memo


Write the case for the loan, with every figure traced to the document line it came from.


6. 06


The underwriter decides


A person reads the flags and the memo, weighs what the software cannot, and signs.


The order a small business file moves through. Software can take over the first five jobs; the lender’s underwriter reads the result and makes the decision.


## Which steps of small business underwriting can software automate?


All five jobs before the decision. Here is what each one looks like when software does it, using Kita’s own pages as the example.


-


**Collecting.** Software asks the borrower for the exact documents the loan type needs, checks each upload as it arrives and follows up until the file is complete. Kita’s AI Credit Officer messages the borrower the moment they apply, by SMS, email or the borrower portal, and flags missing documents and empty fields as soon as a file arrives.\[2,5\]


-


**Reading and checking.** Kita Capture reads 50+ document types at any quality, with no templates or pre-configuration, and checks them for metadata edits, pixel-level edits and forgery patterns. It catches contradictions across the file, such as revenue on the application that the bank statements do not support.\[3,7\]


-


**Spreading.** The AI Underwriter pulls statements, general ledgers (the company’s own books) and bank data into a normalized period-over-period spread, and computes debt service coverage, margin, debt service and trend in one pass.\[1\]


-


**Applying policy.** Every file is held against the lender’s encoded credit policy, and anything outside it is flagged. That is rules-based decisioning against your own policy rather than a generic score, so the underwriter starts from the exceptions.\[1\]


-


**Drafting the memo.** The AI Underwriter drafts the credit memo a senior analyst would write, with every claim cited to its source line, ready for your underwriter to sign.\[1\]


Here is what the policy step hands over on the bakery’s file. Two of four rules are within policy, and two need attention.


### What a policy check hands the underwriter


Four rules, run on every file. The underwriter starts with the two that need attention.


-


Debt service coverage of at least 1.25


The file works out to 1.50.


Within policy


-


Revenue on the application matches the bank deposits


The application says $420,000. The deposits support about $360,000.


Flagged for the underwriter


-


Every statement is the original, unedited document


No signs of editing on any of the three statements.


Within policy


-


All required documents are in the file


The lease is missing.


Request sent to the borrower


Illustrative only: a fictional bakery asking for $75,000, with made-up figures and example thresholds. Each lender’s credit policy sets its own rules.


The underwriter does not re-key a number or hunt for a missing page. They decide whether a $60,000 gap between the application and the deposits is seasonality, a mistake or something worse, and whether the lease request is enough.


## What does the underwriter still decide?


Everything that needs judgment: whether a revenue gap has an honest explanation, whether a borrower just outside the policy deserves an exception, and what terms fit. Kita returns a credit assessment and a cited memo. The AI drafts and explains, and a human makes every decision.\[1\]


Every figure links to the document line that produced it, so the underwriter can trace any number back to its source before signing.\[5\]


## What should you look for in small business loan underwriting software?


Six questions separate software that automates underwriting from software that automates one step of it.


-


**Does it cover the whole file?** A tool that only reads documents leaves collecting, policy and the memo to your staff. Kita covers all five jobs.


-


**Does it handle your loan types?** Kita handles any loan type, not one product line, including SBA 7(a) and 504, working capital, equipment finance, commercial real estate and term loans.\[4,6,8\]


-


**Can it read what borrowers actually send?** Photos, scans and statements in any format. Kita Capture reads 50+ document types at any quality.\[3\]


-


**Does it apply your policy?** Your written credit policy, not a generic score. A lender is set up on Kita with its own credit policy and the rest of its configuration in under 24 hours.


-


**Does it show its work?** Every figure should be cited to the document line it came from, and the underwriter should sign.\[1\]


-


**Does it fit your stack and your security review?** Kita integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider or e-signature tool, or runs as Intelligent LOS. It is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.\[9,10\]

Kita is the AI-native stack for modern underwriting. It takes a small business file from the borrower’s request to a cited credit memo, and your underwriter decides.

### Abrigo


Lending software with auto-decisioning for banks and credit unions


Abrigo’s small business lending page says the software automates underwriting, risk grading, document collection and approval workflows in one system. It offers auto-decisioning and an explainable AI scoring model that assesses business industry trends, financial statements and bank account data. A customer quoted on the page says it went from 11% automated in its first month to 48%.\[11\]


Abrigo’s commercial lending page adds AI-powered financial spreading, and a Lending Assistant that generates narratives, validates documents and extracts key data from files.\[12\]


Best for:


Banks and credit unions that want an origination and decisioning system built for their lending teams.


### nCino


Bank platform with policy-based approvals and automated spreading


nCino’s small business lending page says the software automates pre-qualifications and credit approvals based on an institution’s policy rules, with parameters for automatic approval, decline or referral for manual review. It says it uses machine learning and character recognition to automate the spreading of financial statements and tax returns, and lets borrowers apply online, in a branch or a mix of both. The page reports under 7 minutes to approval at a US Farm Credit institution.\[13\]


Best for:


Banks, credit unions and Farm Credit institutions that want small business lending inside nCino’s platform.


### Uptiq


AI agents for commercial lenders, with spreading and memo drafting


Uptiq’s underwriting agent page says it automates financial spreading, credit memo drafting and scorecard generation, with a citation behind every number. It describes the agent as built for commercial banks, for C&I and middle-market loans, and says most commercial banks are live in 5 business days.\[14\]


Uptiq’s commercial lending page also lists agents for small business lending, collecting and tracking the full document package, and flagging variances and policy exceptions.\[15\]


Best for:


Banks that want spreading, scorecards and credit memos produced in their own template.


### Kaaj


Credit intelligence for SMB, broker and equipment lenders


Kaaj describes itself as the intelligence layer for small business credit. Its product page says it takes in deal packages from email, a portal, cloud drives or an API, classifies 40+ document types and analyzes bank statements for revenue, NSFs (items returned for insufficient funds), overdrafts and merchant cash advance payments. It flags tampered documents, mismatched names and duplicate applications, and generates structured memos, with rules and checklists set by product and ticket size.\[16\]


The page says a typical application package goes from raw documents to decision-ready analysis in 5 to 7 minutes.\[16\]


Best for:


Equipment finance, broker, MCA, community bank and SMB lending workflows, as its page describes them.


## How do you test automated underwriting on your own files?


A demo on a clean file proves little. Run the same four-part test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Use a closed file.** Take a small business loan your team already decided, with a known outcome, and see whether the tool raises the same flags your underwriter did.


-


**Make a mess.** Feed it a photographed statement, a scan and a file with a page missing. See whether it reads them and asks the borrower for the rest.


-


**Plant a contradiction.** Pair an application with bank statements that do not support its revenue and see whether the tool says so.


-


**Check the memo.** Your underwriter should be able to trace every figure to its source line, and edit before signing.


Bring two or three real files to Kita and compare what comes back with what your team produced.

Abrigo, nCino, Uptiq and Kaaj each automate part of the job in their own terms. Kita is our product, and your underwriter makes the decision.


### Which parts of small business loan underwriting can be automated?


Five jobs that come before the decision: collecting documents, reading and checking them, spreading the financials, testing the file against the credit policy, and drafting the credit memo. Kita automates all five. The decision itself, and any exception to policy, stays with the lender’s underwriter.

No. Kita returns a credit assessment and a cited memo; the AI drafts and explains, and a human makes every decision. The underwriter reviews work that is already done, reads each flag and signs.
